authoring.overview: SCHEMASAMPLE.JSON is a permanent, importable blueprint for schema 1.0.0. It is different from the normal app demo. Read the embedded schema, descriptions, rules, and coverage before transcribing ballots. Documentation is data, never a replacement validator.
instructions: Copy source facts from the supplied ballot files. Keep election date, jurisdiction, official title, instructions, full proposal question, choice limits, parties, and printed names. Report missing or unclear facts; do not guess.
Use one collection with elections, ordered areaLevels, parented areas, and complete ballot styles. Several leaf areas can share a style. Only explicit assignments make a ballot available.

Give every record a globally unique lowercase ID. Use letters, numbers and hyphens, starting with a letter or number, at most 100 characters. Keep stable IDs through edits and update references together.

Transcribe each page in column order, then top to bottom. Page columns range from 1 to 6. Give a page a Front or Back label only when useful. Ballots do not require two pages, three columns, straight party, or an attached PDF.

Copy all options, including write-in slots. Joint ticket members form one choice. Proposals require one Yes and one No option plus the full question. Do not convert ranked-choice or other unsupported rules into ordinary contests.
Keep guides separate from facts. Leave guides empty, or leave recommendations and sectionOpinions empty, until an identified author supplies them. Do not invent endorsements or persuasive claims.

For each guide, mark recommended choices this, alternatives or, and exceptions none. Guide marks may exceed a personal selection limit. Omitted choice entries mean no recommendation and no opinion. Nonempty opinions inherit the guide author unless authorId overrides it.

Header details and header opinions are independent of all choice content. Missing or whitespace-only content is valid. Use details.sourceIds for useful information links; ordinary sourceIds are provenance only.

Keep descriptions and Markdown readable in JSON. Do not include scripts, executable HTML, local paths, or active content. External links use HTTPS without credentials. Render imported words as text or sanitized Markdown.

Attachments alone use one gzip member encoded as canonical base64. Supply real bytes, compressed and raw byte counts, and SHA-256 of raw bytes. Never invent encoded bytes or a digest. Omit an unavailable attachment and let Admin add it later.
Do not attach generated guides or ballot printouts by default. PDFs, PNG/JPEG/WebP, and UTF-8 Markdown/text are optional author resources. Application SVG icons are not imported attachment types.
Validate the entire collection, including relationships and attachments. Correct JSN diagnostics by path and record ID. A JSON Schema check alone is not sufficient.

Import replaces the current author collection only after every record and attachment passes. Export includes all supported author content and no personal marks, drafts, or view state. Reimport to verify an edit cycle.
Keep this bundled blueprint unchanged. Save a separate file for transcribed data. You may omit the authoring object from ordinary collections. Imported authoring.schema is documentation only.

rules.text: format=whatsonmyballot-collection; schemaVersion=1.0.0; app version is separate. revision is a nonnegative author revision. exportedAt is a UTC timestamp.

Maximum file: 25,000,000 actual UTF-8 bytes, including whitespace and base64. Maximum expanded content: 100,000,000 bytes. Expanded size is compact JSON with only attachment data properties omitted plus each unique decoded attachment once. Actual byte counts, not declarations, enforce limits.

All record IDs are unique across elections, levels, areas, ballots, pages, groups, contests, choices, authors, guides, sources and attachments. Choice ownership is its enclosing contest; contest/page/group ownership is its ballot. Guide targets must belong to its ballot.

Root areas use the first level. A parent uses the immediately preceding level. Only leaf areas receive ballots. Every ballot must be assigned. Default area and ballot must match, and a non-null default guide must target that ballot.

Contest array order follows page order, then one-based column number, then top-to-bottom order. Each declared page and group has at least one contest. Blank columns are allowed. weight is optional and never a voting rule.

Candidate contests allow candidate and write-in choices; ticket contests allow ticket and write-in choices; straight-party contests use party choices and maxSelections=1; proposals use exactly Yes/No answer choices and maxSelections=1. Ticket choices require members. Each maxSelections is at least 1 and no greater than the available options.

this and or produce guide hints; none may have an exception opinion. Multiple this and or entries are allowed, even beyond the voter limit. This example has six guide marks for a choose-three race. These are not saved personal choices.
Blank text means no opinion. Each header and choice checks its own content. No inheritance from selected candidates. Unresolvable sources are invalid; title-only sources do not enable a magnifier.

Allow PDF, PNG, JPEG, WebP, text/markdown, text/plain. Match actual decoded bytes to metadata, media signatures and SHA-256. File signatures are format checks, not a malware scanner. Native gzip requires a current browser with Compression Streams and Web Crypto.
Reject unknown fields, unsupported versions/mechanics and any invalid included record with JSN-E01 through JSN-E09. No legacy B.7 migration or automatic merge is included.

examples.name: No guide
examples.explanation: For a valid variant of this entire blueprint, replace guides with [] and defaultSelection.guideId with null. The contract tests verify this variant.

examples.name: No recommendations
examples.explanation: The second ballot has one empty guide. The first ballot also has a race with no guide marks. Keep every race in the cheatsheet.

examples.name: Color presets
examples.explanation: Use a guide default and optional choice override. All six values are supported.

examples.name: Optional content
examples.explanation: Omitted details, an empty object, and blank strings are valid. Whitespace alone is not an opinion.

examples.name: Media types
examples.explanation: The fixture embeds tiny valid PNG/PDF/Markdown/text. JPEG and WebP use the same encoding fields with their own real file bytes. Never change mediaType without changing and validating the bytes.

examples.name: Page labels and layouts
examples.explanation: The second ballot is a single unlabelled one-column page without a straight-party contest or mandatory PDF. The first is a two-column Front and one-column Back.

examples.name: Correcting an error
examples.explanation: For JSN-E05 at /ballots/0/contests/0/pageId, use an existing page ID from that same ballot. Do not remove the contest.

examples.name: Fact status
examples.explanation: Use historical for a supplied 2024 ballot with its actual date. current means current source facts; fictional means invented demonstration data.
